text:
maya: seeing a spike of long-lived gRPC chat streams dropping ~90s after open when they path through edge-proxy in us-west-2. clients report mid-conversation cut, server shows EOF
sandeep: ugh, 90s smells like an idle timeout or conntrack NAT expiry. where are these streams exiting? edge gw -> alb -> k8s svc?
jordan: correct flow: client -> cloud-cdn (edge-proxy) -> ALB (nlb with proxy protocol) -> envoy sidecar -> app. Only reproduces when edge-proxy present.
nina: can you paste server logs (grpc-go) and any envoy/edge logs?
maya: paste few lines: 
```
grpc: transport: http2Server.HandleStreams failed to read frame: readFrame header: read tcp 10.0.1.5:443: connection reset by peer
rpc: stream error: code = Canceled desc = "context canceled"
```

sandeep: envoy logs around same time? specifically GOAWAY or RST_STREAM frames?
maya: envoy shows repeated: 
```
[warning] h2: received GOAWAY (debug=0x0, err=NO_ERROR), last_stream_id=15
[info] draining connection, id=0x45
```

jordan: interesting — GOAWAY without error. ALB or CDN might be ending connection due to stream-level buffering or perceived idle. What are idle timeout settings on the edge-proxy?
maya: default edge-proxy idle_timeout is 60s, but this is 90s observed (maybe extra hops). ALB idle is 120s. conntrack showing 90s?
sandeep: ran conntrack dump from a node: 
```
proto=6 src=10.12.0.34 dst=34.217.x.y sport=52344 dport=443 state=ESTABLISHED timeout=89
```

nina: that timeout=89 definitely lines up. NAT conntrack from our egress gateway looks low. edge-proxy reuses keepalive pings? grpc/HTTP2 expects long-lived streams with periodic data, but if no frames for 90s conntrack drops and TCP RST occurs.
jordan: are we using proxy-protocol? NAT table counts per 5-tuple; if CDN terminates and re-establishes upstream, the conntrack entries at edge egress could be getting stale.
ops-bot: incident created: INF-2026-43. Notified @oncall.
@oncall: looking now. quick mitigation: enable HTTP/2 pings (keepalive) from client or bump conntrack timeout on egress. Which is lower risk?
sandeep: bumping conntrack globally is risky but faster. Could also enable envoy h2_connection_keepalive and set keepalive_timeout to 120s so periodic WINDOW_UPDATE/PNs keep conn alive.
maya: can we test a config change in staging? jenkins job to roll proxies?
jordan: yes, create k8s patch for edge-proxy daemonset to set: 
```
--http2-keepalive-interval=30s
--http2-keepalive-timeout=10s
```
and adjust conntrack on egress NAT SG: sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=3600 for a small ring.
nina: note: AWS-managed NAT GW has hard limits; we control our egress nodes only for private NAT. If traffic goes via managed nat gateway, can't change conntrack there. Need to confirm which path the failing flows use.
maya: repro script: 
```
grpcurl -import-path ./proto -plaintext -d '{"msg":"ping"}' -H "te: trailers" -max-time 200 host:443 service.Chat/Stream
```
I can repro in prod with same behavior when requests route via cloud-cdn.
sandeep: run tcpdump on edge-proxy node for that flow to see FIN/RST origin. If conntrack times out, RST originates from our node when it tries to reuse ephemeral ports.
jordan: suggestion for immediate prod mitigation: 1) configure edge-proxy to send periodic HTTP/2 pings/keepalive (30s) 2) open a limited-scope change to increase conntrack timeout on egress hostpool (only nodes in egress role) 3) add CloudWatch alarm for conntrack table usage.
maya: I'll open PR for proxy config and a runbook to rollback.
ops-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood.internal/edge/proxy-config/pull/312
nina: longer-term we should ensure upstream LB preserves client IPs (so conntrack not needed) or use TLS passthrough for chat streams. That will reduce NAT footprint.
sandeep: agree. Also we should add an integration test in chaos lab that holds long-lived streams through the whole path for >10min.
jordan: can someone own the rollout? maya take lead for the config change, sandeep take conntrack patch, nina look at LB passthrough feasibility.
maya: ack, will roll config in staging now. will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
